headline_marked: [[Citrix NetScaler RCE flaws attacked before a fix existed]]: two critical edge vulnerabilities rated 9.5 CVSS v4
headline: Citrix NetScaler RCE flaws attacked before a fix existed: two critical edge vulnerabilities rated 9.5 CVSS v4
summary: Citrix has released emergency patches for two NetScaler remote code execution vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, which were actively exploited in the wild.
details: Citrix published fixes for two NetScaler flaws on September 27, 2026, after watchTowr reported unpatched remote code execution bugs under active exploitation. Both critical flaws are rated 9.5 under CVSS v4, indicating severe impact.

CVE-2026-88771 is an improper input validation vulnerability allowing unauthenticated attackers to run arbitrary commands on all NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway deployments. CVE-2026-88772 is a memory overflow that can lead to remote code execution or denial of service, affecting appliances with DTLS enabled, which is default for VPN virtual servers.

watchTowr stated on September 26, 2026, that it was responding to credible reports of unpatched NetScaler RCE issues, later confirming the flaws were found during forensic investigations. Citrix observed exploits of both CVEs on unmitigated deployments, meaning they were used before any public fix existed.

Appliances on versions 14.1-73.32 and 13.1-63.21, which previously fixed an August authentication bypass, are within the affected range and require this new update. NetScaler ADC and Gateway devices are typically deployed at the network edge, handling critical functions like VPN, remote access, and load balancing.

Citrix's bulletin lists no workaround and no indicators of compromise for the exploited flaws. Because exploitation preceded disclosure, patching restores safety but does not confirm whether an attacker already established access. Administrators should preserve authentication and VPN logs before applying changes, then actively hunt for anomalous command execution and outbound connections.

As of September 30, 2026, ZoomEye identified 239,277 assets matching the "Citrix NetScaler" fingerprint globally. This figure counts potential matches, not confirmed vulnerable appliances, as the affected configuration still needs per-device verification.

headline_marked: Apple [[now accepting iPhone Duo app submissions]] built with Xcode 27.1
headline: Apple now accepting iPhone Duo app submissions built with Xcode 27.1
summary: Developers can now submit apps optimized for the upcoming iPhone Duo using Xcode 27.1, signaling that the device's launch is imminent.
details: Apple has officially opened the App Store for submissions of applications optimized for the highly anticipated iPhone Duo. Developers are encouraged to build and submit their apps using the latest Xcode 27.1. This move strongly suggests that the launch of the iPhone Duo is fast approaching.
caption:
